claims.note: No listed source states the union or nilable syntax: reference/ is the book's table of contents (only a 'Union types' nav entry), /api/ a class index, /docs/ a 485-byte redirect stub, shards a dependency-manager README. The unlisted reference/1.22/syntax_and_semantics/type_grammar.html (fetched today) says 'alias Int32OrNil = Int32? is the same as: alias Int32OrNil = Int32 | ::Nil'.

No listed page covers generic, metaclass or self type syntax. The unlisted type_grammar.html (fetched today) shows 'Array(String)' under 'Regular types and generics can be used', plus Int32.class and self, but never a Hash(String, Int32) example; that form appears only on the equally unlisted typeof.html (':: Hash(Int32, String)').

claims.claim: Tuple `{Int32, String}`; NamedTuple `{a: Int32}`; Proc `Int32, String -> Bool` (shorthand) or `Proc(Int32, String, Bool)`.
claims.note: No listed page documents tuple, named tuple or proc type syntax. The unlisted type_grammar.html (fetched today) states 'alias Int32StringTuple = {Int32, String} is the same as: Tuple(Int32, String)' and shows '{x: Int32, y: String}' and 'Int32, Char -> String' - same forms as the skill, different example keys and proc types.

No listed page documents pointer or static array type syntax. The unlisted type_grammar.html (fetched today) states 'alias Int32Ptr = Int32* is the same as: alias Int32Ptr = Pointer(Int32)' and 'alias Int32_8 = Int32[8] is the same as: StaticArray(Int32, 8)' - the equivalence holds, but the skill's Int32[4] example appears on no fetched page.

claims.claim: `typeof(a, b)` gives the union of both at compile time and does not execute the expression.
claims.note: No listed page documents typeof's behaviour - the reference index has only a 'typeof' nav entry and /api/ a Crystal::Macros::TypeOf index entry. The unlisted typeof.html (fetched today) says 'It accepts multiple arguments, and the result is the union of the expression types' and 'Since typeof doesn't actually evaluate the expression, it can be used on methods at compile time'.

claims.claim: `Foo?` binds tighter than `|`, so `Int32 | String?` is `Int32 | String | Nil`.
claims.note: 'binds', 'tighter' and 'precedence' appear zero times in every fetched page, listed or unlisted; neither type_grammar.html nor union_types.html states how ? interacts with |. The substance may well be true, but no source I could find says so - cite one or drop the gotcha.

claims.claim: `T.class` expressions in generic restrictions need `.class`, e.g. `x : T.class`.
claims.note: No listed source covers free-variable .class restrictions. The unlisted type_restrictions.html (fetched today) says 'To create a method that accepts a type name, rather than an instance of a type, append .class to a free variable in the type restriction' with the example 'def foo(x : T.class) forall T'.

claims.claim: `x.class` is the runtime class, `typeof(x)` the compile-time type.
claims.note: No listed source contrasts .class with typeof. The unlisted type_grammar.html covers Int32.class as referring to 'a class type, instead of an instance type' and the unlisted typeof.html the compile-time behaviour, but no fetched page states the runtime-vs-compile-time contrast in these words.

'eval' appears zero times in the four listed pages. The unlisted compiler man page reference/1.22/man/crystal/index.html (fetched today) documents 'crystal eval : eval code from args or standard input', so the command is real but uncited by any listed source.
